title: Canonical evaluation — cross-day reproducible contract for the headline metrics in docs/evaluation.md §3
why_end_date_is_pinned: With end_date unset the simulator anchors the 30-day window to *today* 00:00 UTC (app/simulator/engine.py), so the same seed yields a one-day-shifted dataset on a different calendar day (docs/evaluation.md §1). Pinning 2026-08-28 — the anchor the historical canonical run_b371e5b4 resolved to on its run day — freezes the window: same code + same spec reproduces the same dataset on any day.

dataset.run_id_note: The simulator_run_id embeds the config hash, which now includes the pinned end_date, so it differs from the historical unpinned run's sim_42_50f24b57d0. The dataset CONTENT is identical to run_b371e5b4's (same seed, same anchor): every data-derived metric matches exactly (see verification.expected). Entity ids embed the run id, so id-keyed randomization — holdout assignment (sha256 over customer id) and per-payment conversion draws — re-keys versus the historical run; draw-derived numbers (opportunity count, recovered revenue, lift point) legitimately differ from run_b371e5b4. The spec's bit-reproducibility claim is run-to-run of THIS spec, not bit-identity with the historical unpinned run.

versions.harness_note: Verified on the working tree at this sha plus the additive --end-date/run-record changeset (scripts/run_evaluation.py, app/services/evaluation/runner.py, tests/evaluation/test_reproducibility.py); the changeset alters no simulator, detection, diagnosis, policy, or conversion logic. If any recorded version moves, expect metric movement and investigate — that is the spec doing its job.

verification.method: Three consecutive executions of `command`, each against its own scratch database (backend/artifacts/repro/canonical_{1,2,3.db}, gitignored), stored metrics diffed pairwise with only wall-clock MTTR stripped (metrics.mean_time_to_recover_minutes, metrics.arms.pulsecover.mttr_minutes).
verification.result: Pairwise-identical stored metrics across all three runs with exactly two documented exception classes: (a) wall-clock MTTR (an operational pipeline measurement, not a simulator output; happened to coincide at 0.0005 min in all three runs), (b) last-bit float wobble in up to two stored diagnosis confidences per pair (e.g. 0.4796502975443439 vs 0.47965029754434385) — the same 17th-significant-digit serialization phenomenon docs/evaluation.md §1 already discloses. No draw, count, rate, revenue figure, or CI differs.
verification.anchor_flow_proof: Same harness, tiny scale (upi_outage_demo, seed 11, days 2, events 1200, customers 60), one run per --end-date into backend/artifacts/repro/anchor_flow.db: --end-date 2026-08-20 -> stored anchor 2026-08-20T00:00:00+00:00, dataset_version sim_11_75ecab6ca2@2026-08-20; --end-date 2026-08-21 -> stored anchor 2026-08-21T00:00:00+00:00, dataset_version sim_11_b4437152cf@2026-08-21. The stored record moves with the pin.

expected.comment: Data-derived values every spec run must reproduce while the recorded versions hold; draw-derived values (opportunities, recovered revenue, lift) are bit-stable across spec runs but NOT equal to the historical unpinned run (see dataset.run_id_note).

tests: backend/tests/evaluation/test_reproducibility.py — end_date plumbing reaches the simulator config, the stored run record carries all version/anchor fields, two same-pin runs are bit-identical (wall-clock MTTR stripped).
